Get started with persephone3

Source: vignettes/persephone3.Rmd
persephone3.Rmd

Introduction

persephone3 provides an object-oriented wrapper around the seasonal adjustment packages in the rjdverse, specifically rjd3x13 and rjd3tramoseats. The package performs time series adjustments using the Java library JDemetra+ with a focus on batch processing, hierarchical time series, and interactive visualizations.

Installation

Install persephone3 and its dependencies from GitHub:

# Install rjdverse dependencies first
remotes::install_github("rjdverse/rjd3toolkit@*release")
remotes::install_github("rjdverse/rjd3x13@*release")
remotes::install_github("rjdverse/rjd3tramoseats@*release")

# Install persephone3
remotes::install_github("statistikat/persephone3")

Basic Workflow

Creating a Seasonal Adjustment Object

The first step is to create a seasonal adjustment object using either perX13() for X-13ARIMA-SEATS or perTramo() for TRAMO/SEATS:

library(persephone3)
#> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'quantmod':
#>   method            from
#>   as.zoo.data.frame zoo
# X-13ARIMA-SEATS with default rsa3 template
obj_x13 <- perX13(AirPassengers)
obj_x13
#> A persephone object
#> Not yet run.

# TRAMO/SEATS with default template
obj_tramo <- perTramo(AirPassengers)
obj_tramo
#> A persephone object
#> Not yet run.

The template argument determines the default specification. Available templates differ between X-13 and TRAMO/SEATS:

X-13ARIMA-SEATS Templates (perX13())

Template Log/Level Detection Outlier Detection Calendar Effects ARIMA Model
rsa0 None None None Airline (+mean)
rsa1 Automatic AO, LS, TC None Airline (+mean)
rsa2c Automatic AO, LS, TC 2 TD vars + Easter Airline (+mean)
rsa3 Automatic AO, LS, TC None Automatic
rsa4 Automatic AO, LS, TC 2 TD vars + Easter Automatic
rsa5c Automatic AO, LS, TC 7 TD vars + Easter Automatic

Default: "rsa3"

See rjd3x13::x13_spec() for details.

TRAMO/SEATS Templates (perTramo())

Template Log/Level Detection Outlier Detection Calendar Effects ARIMA Model
rsa0 None None None Airline (+mean)
rsa1 Automatic AO, LS, TC None Airline (+mean)
rsa2 Automatic AO, LS, TC 2 TD vars + Easter Airline (+mean)
rsa3 Automatic AO, LS, TC None Automatic
rsa4 Automatic AO, LS, TC 2 TD vars + Easter Automatic
rsa5 Automatic AO, LS, TC 7 TD vars + Easter Automatic
rsafull Automatic AO, LS, TC Automatic Automatic

Default: "rsa3" for perTramo(), "rsa5" for tramoseats_spec()

See rjd3tramoseats::tramoseats_spec() for details.

Abbreviations: - AO: Additive Outlier - LS: Level Shift - TC: Temporary Change - TD: Trading Day

Running the Model

Execute the seasonal adjustment with the run() method:

obj_x13$run()

After running, you can access the results through various methods.

Inspecting Results

Print and rjd3 SA-Output 

# Print object information
obj_x13

#>  run  method type   seasonality logTransform arimaMdl       nOutliers

# Access the rjd3 output object
obj_x13$output

Visualization

persephone3 provides multiple visualization options:

# dygraphs plot method
obj_x13$plot()

# Highcharter interactive plot
hchart(obj_x13)

Other Available Plots

Additional visualization methods are available:

  • obj$plotSpectrum(): Spectral plots
  • obj$plotSeasIrrCal(): Seasonal, irregular, and calendar effects
  • obj$plotResiduals(): Residual diagnostics (ACF, PACF, QQ, histogram)
  • obj$plotSiRatios(): Seasonal-to-Irregular ratio plot

For detailed documentation on all plotting options, see vignette("persephone-plotting").

Customizing Parameters

Parameter Structure

persephone3 provides a unified interface to the underlying rjd3toolkit and rjd3x13 specification functions. Parameters are organized into spec-blocks, where each block corresponds to a specific {rjd3*} function.

The parameter name format is:

block.parameter
  • block: The first part (before the dot) indicates the spec-block and maps to an {rjd3*} function
  • parameter: The second part (after the dot) specifies the parameter within that block

When you pass parameters to updateParams() or during object creation, persephone3 internally routes them to the appropriate {rjd3*} function based on the block name.

Updating Parameters

Use updateParams() to modify seasonal adjustment settings. Parameters are passed directly and mapped to the corresponding {rjd3*} functions:

# Disable log transformation and enable iterative estimation
obj_x13$updateParams(
  transform.fun = "None",
  arima.p = 1,
  arima.d = 2,
  arima.q = 0,
  arima.bp = 1,
  arima.bd = 1,
  arima.bq = 0
)
#> Warning in set_arima.default(x$regarima, ...): autmodel enabled: the
#> parameters will not impact the final parameters

# Re-run with new parameters
obj_x13$run()

# Check updated diagnostics
obj_x13$diagnosticsTable()
#>   component  run method   type seasonality normality independence
#> 1           TRUE    x13 single     Present      Good    Uncertain
#>   QS_seas F_seas combSA_all combSA_last combI_all combI_last
#> 1    Good   Good       Good        Good      Good       Good
#>   fTestSA_td TD_Ftest logTransform       arimaMdl nOutliers    Q   Q2
#> 1     Severe       NA        FALSE (0 1 1)(0 1 0)      Good 0.47 0.53
#>   TotalQ
#> 1 Severe

Available Spec-Blocks

Each spec-block corresponds to a specific function in rjd3toolkit or rjd3x13. You can pass parameters directly using the block.parameter notation, and persephone3 will route them to the appropriate {rjd3*} function:

Block {rjd3*} Function Package Description
arima set_arima() rjd3toolkit ARIMA model specification
automdl set_automodel() rjd3toolkit Automatic model selection
basic set_basic() rjd3toolkit Basic settings (series type, frequency, etc.)
easter set_easter() rjd3toolkit Easter effect adjustment
estimate set_estimate() rjd3toolkit Estimation settings
setout set_outlier() rjd3toolkit Outlier detection settings
td set_tradingdays() rjd3toolkit Trading day effects
transform set_transform() rjd3toolkit Log/Box-Cox transformation
addout add_outlier() rjd3toolkit Add specific outliers
remout remove_outlier() rjd3toolkit Remove outliers
addramp add_ramp() rjd3toolkit Add ramp adjustments
remramp remove_ramp() rjd3toolkit Remove ramp adjustments
usrdefvar add_usrdefvar() rjd3toolkit Add user-defined variables
x11 set_x11() rjd3x13 X-11 specific options (X-13 only)
benchmarking set_benchmarking() rjd3toolkit Benchmarking settings

Note: The parameter names you use in persephone3 (e.g., arima.p, transform.fun) correspond to the argument names in the underlying {rjd3*} functions. For complete parameter documentation, refer to the linked {rjd3*} function documentation.

Simplified Syntax for Some parameters

For certain parameters (e.g., outliers), persephone3 provides a simplified syntax. Instead of using addout.type = c("AO","LS") and addout.date = c("1953-07-01","1954-06-01"), you can write:

obj_x13$updateParams(
  outliers = c("AO1953.7", "LS1954.6")
)
obj_x13$run()

This combines the outlier type and date into a single, more intuitive format.

Accessing Specific Results

Preprocessing Results 

# Access preprocessing output
obj_x13$output$preprocessing
#> Log-transformation: no 
#> SARIMA model: (0,1,1) (0,1,0)
#> 
#> SARIMA coefficients:
#> theta(1) 
#>   -0.256 
#> 
#> Regression model:
#> AO (1960-03-01) 
#>          -43.98 
#> 
#> For a more detailed output, use the 'summary()' function.

Original Series 

# Original series
orig_series <- obj_x13$ts
head(orig_series)
#>      Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun
#> 1949 112 118 132 129 121 135

Seasonally Adjusted Series 

# Get seasonally adjusted series
sa_series <- obj_x13$adjusted
head(sa_series)
#>           Jan      Feb      Mar      Apr      May      Jun
#> 1949 127.4149 126.3824 124.1177 128.1166 127.5550 124.1789

Access Original, Seasonally Adjusted and Trend Series via {rjd3*} user_defined Slot 

# Original series
head(obj_x13$output$user_defined$y)
#>      Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun
#> 1949 112 118 132 129 121 135
# Seasonally adjusted
head(obj_x13$output$user_defined$sa)
#>           Jan      Feb      Mar      Apr      May      Jun
#> 1949 127.4149 126.3824 124.1177 128.1166 127.5550 124.1789
# Trend
head(obj_x13$output$user_defined$t)
#>           Jan      Feb      Mar      Apr      May      Jun
#> 1949 127.1220 126.6891 126.3950 125.9305 125.2265 124.6092

Common Issues

Java not found

If you encounter Java-related errors, ensure Java 17+ is installed:

# Check Java installation
Sys.getenv("JAVA_HOME")

Model convergence issues

If the model fails to converge:

  1. Try a simpler template (e.g., "rsa0" instead of "rsa3")
  2. Disable automatic outlier detection
  3. Check for extreme values or missing data in your series

Repository

Source code and issue tracker: https://github.com/statistikat/persephone3
